shipped_originals.title_o: For everyday arguments prior beliefs play a larger role on perceived argument quality than argument quality itself

blind_target.title: The Everyday Belief Bias: Belief in the Claim of a Political Argument Predicts the Perceived Quality of the Argument.
blind_target.evidence_quote: We also replicate the belief consistency effect found previously in the Everyday Belief Bias Task (Deans-Browne & Singmann, 2024); participants think arguments are of better quality if the arguments are also in line with their beliefs.
blind_target.outcome_quote: We also replicate the belief consistency effect found previously in the Everyday Belief Bias Task (Deans-Browne & Singmann, 2024); participants think arguments are of better quality if the arguments are also in line with their beliefs. We also replicate that the maximum belief bias effect was larger than the largest effect of argument type (i.e., the average difference in argument quality ratings between good and authority-based arguments). Furthermore, we replicated the failure to find a linear or quadratic interaction between argument type and belief consistency, suggesting that the effect of argument type is somewhat similar irrespective of how in line the argument is with an individual’s belief.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly confirm belief consistency, its greater magnitude than argument type, and the original absence of the interaction. The new comparison between types of bad argument is an extension.

shipped_originals.title_o: The Prevention, Identification, and Cognitive Determinants of Math Difficulty.
shipped_originals.authors_o: Fuchs; Compton; Fuchs; Paulsen; Bryant; Hamlett

blind_target.evidence_quote: Replication studies are extremely rare in education. This randomized controlled trial (RCT) is a scale-up replication of Fuchs et al., which in a sample of 139 found a statistically significant positive impact for Number Rockets, a small-group intervention for at-risk first graders that focused on building understanding of number operations.
blind_target.outcome_quote: Replication studies are extremely rare in education. This randomized controlled trial (RCT) is a scale-up replication of Fuchs et al., which in a sample of 139 found a statistically significant positive impact for Number Rockets, a small-group intervention for at-risk first graders that focused on building understanding of number operations. The study was relatively small scale (one site) and highly controlled. This replication was implemented at a much larger scale—in 76 schools in four urban districts; 994 at-risk students participated. Intervention students participated in approximately 30 hours of small-group work in addition to classroom instruction; control students received typical instruction and whatever assistance the teacher would normally provide. Intervention students showed significantly superior performance on a broad measure of mathematics proficiency.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The abstract states a positive original intervention effect and a significantly superior replication intervention result. Bibliographic details are unavailable in the saved abstract.

shipped_originals.title_o: Significant Linkage of Parkinson Disease to Chromosome 2q36-37
shipped_originals.authors_o: Pankratz; Nichols; Uniacke; Halter; Rudolph; Shults; Conneally; Foroud

blind_target.evidence_quote: Recently, significant linkage has been reported to a 39.5 cM region on the long arm of chromosome 2 (2q36-37; PARK11) in North American Parkinson families under an autosomal dominant model of inheritance. We have performed a replication study to confirm linkage to this region in a European population.
blind_target.outcome_quote: Linkage analysis in 153 individuals from 45 European families with a strong family history of PD did not show any significant LOD score in this region. Therefore, PARK11 does not seem to play a major role for familial PD in the European population.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Explicit replication of previously significant linkage yields no linkage and an overall negative conclusion.
